data.long_meaning: The name Ksenija is of Slavic origin and translates to 'descendant of Xenia'. Xenia was a Greek goddess of hospitality, and the name Ksenija is derived from her name. The name signifies grace and hospitality.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the grace and hospitality of God, inviting others into our lives and homes.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ksenija holds cultural significance in the Slavic region, where hospitality and generosity are highly valued. Ksenija symbolizes warmth, kindness, and welcoming nature. The name has been popular among Slavic Christians, particularly in the Eastern Orthodox Church, where the manifestation of hospitality and love towards others is a significant aspect of the faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ksenija holds spiritual significance as a reflection of the Christian virtues of love, kindness, and hospitality. It symbolizes the call to carry the spirit of Xenia and extend a welcoming hand to all, just as Jesus did. The name serves as a reminder to honor and practice the principle of hospitality towards others, which is essential to nurturing meaningful relationships and fostering a loving community.

historical_references.reference: Ksenija, the daughter of Constantine the Great, was a devoted Christian who played a significant role in the early Christian church. She is said to have built several churches and provided shelter to the poor and needy. Her acts of charity and devotion inspired many in the early Christian community.
historical_references.context: Early Christian period in the Roman Empire

historical_references.reference: Ksenija of Lithuania, also known as Alexandra, was the queen consort of King Sigismund I the Old of Poland in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. She was a devout and learned woman who helped promote the Renaissance in Poland. She was known for her patronage of artists, scholars, and the arts.
historical_references.context: Renaissance period in Poland and Europe
